messages:
luis_customer: Hey team, we've got a blocking issue — embeddings from Dedicated instances are coming back with 1024 dims, but Hosted returns 1536 for the same model/commit. Customers see downstream index errors and search mismatch. Can someone triage?

anna_support: @luis_customer thanks for the report — can you paste a minimal curl (or SDK call) that repros the mismatch and which model alias you called? Also which deployment (region/stack) you're hitting for Dedicated?

luis_customer: Minimal curl:```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood-hosted.example/v1/embeddings \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"open-embed-1536-v2","input":["hello world"]}'
```
Hosted returns JSON with "embedding": [1536 floats]. Dedicated cluster rj-dedicated-01 returns same call (same token, different endpoint) but payload has 1024 floats.

raj_infra: @luis_customer which binary/version is the dedicated runtime running? We've seen quantized variants that change output dim in the past if the wrong model file is loaded. Can you share the model SHA or the registry entry?

luis_customer: Dedicated shows model id: open-embed-1536-v2@sha:aa11bb, Hosted shows same id on the dashboard. Token scope is identical.

maya_ml: Quick idea: tokenizer or model manifest mismatch could lead to truncated vector if a legacy config key like "embed_dim" is present. Also batching differences could hit fallback embedding logic. Do we have inference logs?

luis_customer: I grabbed the Dedicated pod logs (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-10T14:05:02Z] INFO load model: open-embed-1536-v2@aa11bb quantized=false
[2026-03-10T14:05:03Z] WARN model manifest: embed_dim=1024 (deprecated) in /opt/models/manifest.json
[2026-03-10T14:05:03Z] INFO serving endpoint /v1/embeddings ready
[2026-03-10T14:05:03Z] DEBUG kv-cache miss
[2026-03-10T14:05:04Z] INFO request id=xyz embed_dim=1024 input_len=1 batch_size=4 latency=34ms
```

anna_support: That manifest line looks suspicious — we usually expect embed_dim to be absent or set to 1536 for this model. @raj_infra can you check model files on rj-dedicated-01 and whether there's a manifest override?

raj_infra: On it. I ssh'd into rj-dedicated-01 and `cat /opt/models/open-embed-1536-v2/manifest.json` shows:
```
{
  "name": "open-embed-1536-v2",
  "sha": "aa11bb",
  "embed_dim": 1024,
  "quantized": true
}
```

raj_infra: Looks like during a data migration last week a legacy manifest from an older 1024 variant got copied in. The model file is actually the 1536 weights but the manifest says 1024, and our runtime uses manifest.embed_dim to allocate output buffer, so the runtime is slicing the vector.

maya_ml: That explains it. Two immediate remediation paths: 1) Correct the manifest to match the weights (set embed_dim:1536 and quantized=false if appropriate) and restart the runtime (quick). 2) Add a runtime guard to detect mismatch between weight shape and manifest and fail loudly instead of slicing (longer-term).

luis_customer: For blockers, do you recommend we patch manifest ourselves or wait for a coordinated redeploy? We have users timing out on indexing jobs.

anna_support: We can patch now — @raj_infra can you push a corrected manifest and restart the dedicated runtime with minimal downtime? I'll coordinate with the customer for a brief maintenance window.

raj_infra: Doing that now. Steps I used:```bash
# on rj-dedicated-01
sudo cp /opt/models/open-embed-1536-v2/manifest.json /opt/models/open-embed-1536-v2/manifest.json.bak
jq '.embed_dim=1536 | .quantized=false' manifest.json > manifest.fixed.json && mv manifest.fixed.json manifest.json
sudo systemctl restart redwood-inference
```

deploy-bot: deploy started by raj_infra at 2026-03-10T14:12:22Z - rolling restart across podset rj-dedicated-01 (3 pods)

sre_oncall: watching for errors, will alert if latency spikes >2x baseline or error rate >1% for 5m

raj_infra: restart finished on pod1/pod2, pod3 still warm. Logs now show:
```
[2026-03-10T14:13:05Z] INFO load model: open-embed-1536-v2@aa11bb quantized=false
[2026-03-10T14:13:05Z] INFO model manifest verified: embed_dim matches weights (1536)
[2026-03-10T14:13:05Z] INFO request id=abc embed_dim=1536 input_len=1 batch_size=4 latency=38ms
```

luis_customer: Running the same curl now — Hosted and Dedicated outputs both 1536-dim. Indexing resumes. Huge thanks.

maya_ml: Follow-ups: 1) We'll add a CI check when pushing model files to Dedicated that validates manifest vs weights shape. 2) We'll add a warning in the Console if manifest.embed_dim exists for modern models. 3) Consider an emergency parity-check job that compares sample outputs between Hosted/Dedicated/Private periodically.

anna_support: Also flagging this as a potential customer bill impact — they had failed indexing jobs that retried and consumed tokens. @finance should we notify about potential credits? (cc @sre_oncall)

sre_oncall: I'll add a postmortem note and monitor error budgets. No production SLO breach expected since we fixed within ~10min, but we'll record timeline.

luis_customer: One last note — on our Private deployment we had a slightly different symptoms: embeddings were correct dim but values were low-norm after quantized load. We traced that to a mismatch in quantization metadata (scale/zero-point) in the manifest. So manifest integrity checks would have prevented both issues.

raj_infra: Good catch. I'll create a short runbook for customers/operators: checklist to verify when embeddings mismatch across deployments: 1) Confirm model alias+sha on each deployment 2) Check manifest.embed_dim vs weight matrix shape 3) Inspect quantization fields (scale/zero) 4) Run a small canonical test set across envs and compare vector norms and hash of first 8 floats 5) If mismatch, rollback to previous model and open an incident.

maya_ml: I'll file an RFC for runtime guard + CI check. Also adding a tiny test harness to redwoodctl: `redwoodctl model sanity-check --model open-embed-1536-v2 --endpoints hosted,dedicated,private` which returns embedding shape and first-few-floats hash.

anna_support: Marking this resolved with customer ack. I'll follow up on credits privately. Thanks everyone :tada:
